framework_version: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark (control intent; clause numbers not asserted)
source_note: The conditions in this pack are identical to those in the Cisco IOS pack, because both read the same vendor-neutral baseline fields - that is the point of the baseline. What is Junos-specific is the remediation, which is Junos CLI. Clause numbers are deliberately NOT asserted: the control intent below follows the CIS Juniper OS Benchmark, but the exact clause numbering could not be verified against a licensed copy, and inventing one would be worse than omitting it. Map each rule to its clause from your own copy before citing this output in a formal audit.

rules.title: Authenticate device access against a centralised server
rules.description: The device must authenticate administrative access against RADIUS or TACACS+ rather than local accounts alone, with 'system authentication-order' naming the remote method.
rules.rationale: Local-only authentication cannot enforce per-administrator accountability, central credential revocation when someone leaves, or command accounting. On a device reachable from a branch network that is the difference between an audited change and an anonymous one.

remediation.summary: Configure a TACACS+ or RADIUS server and name it in the authentication order, keeping local password as the fallback.

references: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark - centralised authentication
rules.notes: Keep 'password' last in the authentication order so a server outage cannot lock every administrator out. 'commit confirmed' rolls the change back automatically if the session is lost.

rules.title: Offer no cleartext management service under 'system services'
rules.description: Telnet, FTP, finger and xnm-clear-text must not be offered; SSH must be the only interactive management transport.
rules.rationale: Telnet and FTP carry administrative credentials and session content in cleartext. Anyone positioned on a transit segment recovers a privileged password by reading packets, and no other control on the device compensates for that.

remediation.summary: Delete every cleartext service and keep SSH only.
cli: set system services ssh protocol-version v2

references: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark - management plane services
rules.notes: Confirm SSH reachability in a second session before the confirming commit: deleting telnet while SSH is unreachable strands the device.

rules.title: Set a login idle-timeout of 10 minutes or less
rules.description: Every login class must apply an idle timeout, and it must be non-zero and no longer than ten minutes.
rules.rationale: Junos does not time out an idle session unless a timeout is configured, so an unattended terminal keeps a privileged session open indefinitely. An idle timeout is the only control that closes it.

remediation.summary: Apply an idle timeout on the login class used by administrative accounts.
cli: set system login class secure-ops idle-timeout 10
set system login class secure-ops permissions all
set system login user netops class secure-ops

references: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark - idle session timeout
rules.notes: idle-timeout is expressed in minutes on the device; this tool normalizes it to seconds. A value of 0 means 'never' and is treated as a failure, not as an unconfigured value.

rules.title: Protect root with a hashed password and store no plain-text credential
rules.description: 'system root-authentication encrypted-password' must be present, and no plain-text-password statement may appear in the configuration.
rules.rationale: Root is the account that survives every other access control. Without a hashed root credential the device either has no root password or stores a recoverable one, and configuration backups are routinely readable by people who should never hold root.

remediation.summary: Set a root password (Junos prompts and stores it hashed) and pin the hash format.
cli: set system login password format sha512
# Junos prompts for the password and writes it back as encrypted-password

references: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark - root authentication
rules.notes: Junos hashes stored credentials by default and has no equivalent of 'service password-encryption', so this tool reports password_encryption as satisfied unless a plain-text-password statement is actually present in the configuration.

rules.title: Unset the default 'public' and 'private' SNMP communities
rules.description: No SNMP community may be named 'public' or 'private'.
rules.rationale: Default community strings are the first thing an internet-wide scan tries. A read-only 'public' exposes the full interface, route and ARP topology of the device; a read-write 'private' is equivalent to unauthenticated configuration access.

remediation.summary: Delete the default communities; prefer SNMPv3, or at minimum a non-default read-only string restricted by client prefix.

references: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark - SNMP community strings
rules.notes: The trailing 'clients 0.0.0.0/0 restrict' is what actually denies everything not explicitly permitted; without it the client list is advisory.

rules.title: Enforce SSH protocol version 2
rules.description: 'system services ssh protocol-version' must be set to v2.
rules.rationale: SSHv1 has structural flaws - a weak integrity check that permits undetected packet insertion - that no key length or cipher choice repairs. Pinning v2 also removes the negotiated downgrade path.

remediation.summary: Pin the SSH protocol version explicitly rather than relying on the release default.
cli: set system services ssh protocol-version v2
set system services ssh root-login deny

references: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark - SSH protocol version
rules.notes: Releases from Junos 15.1 no longer accept v1 at all, but this tool will not infer the enforced version from a release string: with no protocol-version statement the control is reported as NEEDS_REVIEW rather than assumed compliant.

rules.title: Do not serve J-Web over plain HTTP
rules.description: 'system services web-management http' must not be configured; if J-Web is required it must be served over HTTPS.
rules.rationale: J-Web over HTTP authenticates a full administrative session over an unencrypted channel, so the credential and the session cookie are both recoverable by anyone on the path. The management web interface is also a recurring source of remotely exploitable defects and is rarely needed on an infrastructure device.

remediation.summary: Delete the HTTP listener; serve J-Web over HTTPS only, or remove web management entirely.
cli: set system services web-management https system-generated-certificate
set system services web-management https interface ge-0/0/1.0

references: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark - web management
rules.notes: Bind HTTPS to an inside interface. A system-generated certificate protects the channel but not the identity of the device; use a CA-issued certificate where the management network warrants it.

rules.title: Configure a syslog destination
rules.description: At least one 'system syslog' destination must exist - a remote host, an on-box file, or both.
rules.rationale: Without a log destination there is no record of who logged in, what changed, or when an attack began. Remote syslog additionally survives the device itself being compromised or replaced, which on-box retention does not.

remediation.summary: Send logs to a remote collector and keep a local file as a fallback.
cli: set system syslog host 10.20.30.40 any notice
set system syslog host 10.20.30.40 authorization info
set system syslog file messages any notice
set system syslog file interactive-commands interactive-commands any

references: CIS Juniper OS Benchmark - system logging
rules.notes: 'interactive-commands' records the commands administrators actually ran, which is the log an incident review needs and the one most often missing.
